question: The digit-sum of \(998\) is \(9 + 9 + 8 = 26.\) How many \(3\)-digit whole numbers, whose digit-sum is \(26\), are even?
solution:
An even whole number has an even units digit, so that digit is at most \(8\). The hundreds and tens digits are each at most \(9\). Thus the largest possible digit-sum of a three-digit even number is
\[
9+9+8=26.
\]
To reach 26, all three digits must reach these bounds: making any digit smaller would make the sum less than 26. This forces the number to be \(998\).

Since \(998\) satisfies every condition, there is exactly \(\boxed{1}\) such number, choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
